newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece hands over Turkish warplane pilot.
newsitem.headline: Greece hands over Turkish warplane pilot.

text.p: Greece said on Wednesday it would return a Turkish pilot whose F-16 fighter plane crashed on Tuesday after being intercepted by Greek warplanes near the eastern Aegean island of Chios.
"The pilot will be taken by helicopter to Turkey at 1200 GMT," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.
Greek naval forces rescued the pilot and took him to a hospital on Chios, just off the Turkish coast, after his plane crashed in the Aegean Sea. A search was on for his co-pilot.
The pilot had radioed he was abandoning his plane after being intercepted by two Greek Mirage 2000s. No shots were fired during the interception, Defence Ministry officials said.

The incident occurred on the last day of joint Greek-Cypriot military exercises -- "Nikiforos" on Cyprus and "Toxotis" in the southern Aegean. The exercises stem from a 1993 military pact between Greece and the Cypriot government, which controls the southern, Greek-populated sector of the divided island.

Greece reported more than 50 airspace violations since Monday, when the exercises started. Greek fighter planes were scrambled more than 40 times to intercept Turkish planes on Monday alone, the officials said.
